strengths: The paper addresses a useful problem with an identifiable audience in representation learning, program analysis, and reverse engineering: transferring information from source code and comments into representations usable from low-level code alone.
The anchored encoder and staged contrastive training provide a concrete approach to multimodal transfer. The high-level pipeline is understandable and motivates testable component comparisons.
The reported results are promising across several tasks. Function-name recovery accuracy improves from 29.41 to 33.41, while summarization BLEU-4 improves from GraphCodeBERT’s 32.43 to 34.36.

The manuscript includes component ablations, a CodeT5 extension, positive and negative examples, dataset statistics, and a public data/code archive link. These provide a useful foundation for further investigation.
weaknesses: Necessary: Resolve the POJ-104 evaluation protocol. Section 3.2 and Table 2 specify disjoint sets of 64/16/24 problem labels, whereas Sections 2.3 and 4.2 describe cross-entropy classification into 104 classes. The manuscript does not explain how unseen classes are predicted. Clarify whether this is classification or similarity retrieval, specifying the objective, label mapping, retrieval candidates if applicable, and exact MAP/MAR/MAF1 definitions. Reconcile or rerun the results accordingly. This uncertainty also affects the principal ablations.

Necessary: Align the binary-analysis claims with the evaluated inputs. The experiments use compiler-generated LLVM IR, and Figures 7–8 retain informative function names, callees, and types. Such representations are not trivially interchangeable with stripped executables, as the introductory footnote suggests. Either substantiate the stripped-binary setting with an appropriate preprocessing and evaluation pipeline, or explicitly restrict the claims to compiler-generated LLVM IR.

Necessary: Separate interpolation benefits from additional training. The full model receives 30 or 70 pretraining epochs, versus 10 for PCL; the no-interpolation ablation also receives only 10. The assertion that PCL converged does not sufficiently resolve this confound. A comparable-budget control is needed to attribute improvements to interpolation, and separate linear/nonlinear comparisons are needed for claims about their individual contributions. Alternatively, limit the conclusions to the combined training recipe. Report variability for the key comparisons.

Necessary: Correct the claims about semantic correctness. BLEU, GLEU, and exact match measure textual correspondence and do not establish behavioral preservation. In Figure 8, CONTRABIN’s purportedly positive crypto_alloc_skcipher example omits the &crypto_skcipher_type argument, changing a four-argument call to three arguments. Correct this interpretation and provide compilation/behavioral evidence, or narrow the conclusions to textual reconstruction. Table 6 also shows lower BLEU than GraphCodeBERT (71.14 versus 71.56), with only a 0.43-point exact-match advantage and no uncertainty estimates.

Necessary: Qualify the human-versus-generated-comment conclusions. Table 7’s MAP collapse from 43.78 to 3.11 is striking, but the manuscript does not adequately document matched function coverage, comment extraction, filtering, truncation, or training stability. Length distributions alone cannot establish that verbosity or writing style caused the collapse. Provide controlled evidence or restrict the conclusion to the particular preprocessing configuration tested. The ablation evaluates POJ-104 functionality classification, which does not substantiate the abstract’s broader claim about comprehension tasks.

Necessary: Resolve methodological and reporting inconsistencies. Figure 3 concatenates embeddings, whereas Equations 8 and 10 add them; the permitted interpolation pairs also vary across descriptions. Specify the implemented architecture and gradient flow, including whether Equation 5’s targets are detached. Clarify the AnghaBench split hierarchy and model-selection procedure, since generation results are described as using validation data. Finally, Section 5.1 mislabels relative percentage reductions as point reductions: Table 7’s MAF1 drops are 0.79, 2.85, and 6.97 points, not 2.07, 7.46, and 18.25 points.

Optional: Streamline the repeated human-learning analogies and strengthen the discussion of prior LLVM and binary representation models. Broader compiler and architecture coverage would be useful extensions once the present claims and evaluation protocol are made precise.
